title: Shelve a sweater behind a wardrobe's sliding doors and close them again
instruction: Put the folded sweater on the shelf in the left half of the wardrobe: slide a door to open that half, bring the sweater in through the doorway, never over a door or a wall, then slide the door back so both doors are closed, and let go.
context: Wardrobes with two sliding doors in parallel tracks open only one half at a time: to reach a shelf the right door has to be slid across, the item brought in through the gap, and the door slid back. Robots that tidy clothes away have to work articulated furniture like this and leave it closed, not just place objects on open surfaces.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (bases at y = +30.5 left and -30.5 right): x forward, y to the left, heights above the table top. Fixed, a wooden wardrobe with no top, open towards the arms: side walls 1 cm thick and 16 cm tall with inner faces at y +13.5 and -13.5, running from x 23.2 to the back wall (front face at x 42); a middle divider 1 cm thick (y -0.5 to +0.5) from x 31 to 42, 16 cm tall; in each half a white shelf block from x 31 to 42, 13 cm wide, 5 cm tall (left half y +0.5 to +13.5, right half y -0.5 to -13.5). Four grey floor rails 0.5 cm thick, 1.5 cm tall, across the full inner width: two form the front track (centre x 25) and two the rear track (centre x 29.2), each 0.2 cm clear of its door. Loose: two sliding doors, rigid light wooden panels 1.2 (x) x 14.5 (y) x 12 cm tall, 200 g, standing in the tracks: the front door at y -1 to +13.5 (covering the left half), the rear door at y -13.5 to +1 (covering the right half); each can slide across behind or in front of the other. A folded green wool sweater, a rigid fabric block 8 (x) x 5 (y) x 2.5 cm, 120 g, lying flat on the table at x 16, y +19.
scoring: Hard 0 if at any time the sweater passes over a door or a wardrobe wall or the divider (its footprint overlapping theirs, at any height), if the sweater or a door falls off the table (lowest point more than 5 cm below the table top), or if a door ends out of its track (tilted more than 10 degrees, its underside more than 5 mm off the table, or its centre more than 4 mm off its track's centre line). Otherwise 0.45 with the sweater lying flat (tilt under 10 degrees) and wholly on the left shelf (underside within 5 mm of the shelf top); 0.9 with both doors closed as well (each within 1 cm of its closed position along y). The sweater on the right shelf scores 0. 1.0 requires 0.9, everything still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) and every fingertip of both grippers at least 3 cm from the sweater and the doors, held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. In a real trial, fix the wardrobe and the tracks to the table and keep the arms out of the space above it except through the doorway, as if it had a top. Slide both doors closed and put the sweater back on the table as in the setup.
fidelity: The wardrobe is at about 1/3 scale and has no top, so top-down grippers fit; the rule that the sweater may not pass over a door or wall stands in for the top. The doors are free rigid panels in floor tracks without top guides or rollers. The sweater is a rigid block (no cloth in task files). Friction is the simulator default. Release is checked from fingertip positions by forward kinematics.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left arm reached for the sweater and nudged it about on the table for the full 60 seconds; neither door was opened and the sweater never reached the wardrobe); scripted demo: 1.0 (3 of 3 runs)
